title: Burton's account of a jam session at Paul Mares's house
summary: Perhannis reads Burton's passage about a jam session with Mares, Bix and Wolverines; Moore does not recall it.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I didn't know anything about that. I don't know. In the first place, I wasn't with Paul Whiteman. Oh, oh, no, no. This isn't the one in New Orleans. This is supposed to be in Chicago. Oh, I doubt that. And, uh... In the first place, I think Pauli was back in New Orleans by that time. Uh... Well, probably... Ralph Burton wasn't even sure it was his house, but you... it was a jam session somewhere where Bix came in late, and, uh, several members of the Wolverines were there already. I'm reading part of this. Um... Victor Moore was setting up his drums. Uh... A cheerful, energetic youth with a mop of curly black hair. Uh... Min Lieberk. Lieberk. Lieberk. Lieberk. Uh... Tall, quiet, dreamy, peach-colored chap. Uh... There was Jimmy Hartwell, Bobby Gillette, Dick Bono. Uh... Boynow. Boynow? How do you say that? Boynow. And so... they're saying, where the hell was Bix? Uh... I thought he was with you. And then, don't worry, Bix will be here, Bix said. Apparently there's some dialogue in here. I
don't know whether you—I don't remember them.

And then I guess he finally comes in. At the moment they weren't really rehearsing, just jamming. Mostly Dixieland standards like Panama, Copenhagen, Eccentric, Tiger Rag, Tin Roof, and Pop Tunes. Margie, All By Myself, Hoo, Alabama Bound, Oh Sister Ain't That Hot, Linger A While, The Sheik of Arabia. These things, they stuck to the easier natural keys. C, B flat, E flat, E flat, F natural. They did what? They were stuck to the easier natural keys like C, B flat, E flat, F natural, G natural. Marais got out his horn. Bix sat in and the musical temperature rose perceptibly. Then there was an incident in here of where Bix and Paul Marais exchanged solos. That is, they played off one another, the back and forth, that kind of thing. Like Dylan Miller-Owner. Yeah, exactly. But you don't recall any of that. I don't remember that, if I were even there. Yeah. Have you talked to Ralph Burton at all about him?
No, I haven't. Has he talked to you? No, and I'd like to catch up with him, I can tell you that.
